entry.focal: The hero pavilion as a closed 7 x 7 x 6.5 m dark-brown cube, with a hanging lantern stuck to its outer face like a wall sconce. steps_toro is a white slab at the left edge.
entry.next_visible: No: no sea, no moon, no rail. The deck reads as an empty black plane.

reveal.focal: The pavilion wall 2.5 m away fills the left half; the right half is empty sky with two posts and a bench. Aimed at the moon/sea, the frame shows nothing.

concept.focal: lights1:0 (162.6, 82.2), 0.2 m from the lens, fills the right third as a white slab; the pavilion cube fills the rest.
concept.next_visible: The pool lanterns, faintly, at far left.

strip.focal: Alternates between the pavilion wall and the dark sakura box. Frames 4-7 are an empty dark deck with two posts and a bench.
strip.next_visible: No outward view to sea or moon at any point.

fixes.detail: The 'open pavilion' is graybox-modelled as a solid cube, which swallows the sake_counter, the 8 zabuton and the floor paving and blocks every view east. Replace it with 4 corner posts plus a roof slab from +3.0 to +6.5 m. Shift it 2 m east (to 157, 91) so its open east side frames the sea over the rail, and move east_bench_1/2 to flank it on the rail at y 83 and y 99.

radius 3.6 > the 3.5 half-width, so the lanterns are glued to the outside walls. Use radius 2.9 under the eaves (z about 123.6) with a warm point light each, so the pavilion interior glows and is the brightest thing on the deck, as in 32.
It is 0.2 m from the concept camera (162.5, 82.0). Move it to the rail corner (162.6, 80.8), or move cameras.concept to (160.5, 83.0).
dims 'area: footprint' produced a 4 x 4 m patch under the pavilion only; the 22 x 22 m hinoki deck reads as black ground. Lay the deck over the whole footprint at 120.5.

It is hidden inside the hero box (y 87.9 lies within 87.5-94.5). Put it on the approach side west of the pavilion (about 150.5, 87.9), facing east, as a lit second focal point on the walk in from the steps. If the pavilion becomes an open frame, keeping it inside is also acceptable.

top_change: Open the pavilion and push it to the east rail so the moon and sea are framed through it at eye height; at present the hero is a closed brown cube that blocks the very view the deck exists for.
plausibility: Railings (dressing[0], 12 pieces of 1.5 m at about 5 m pitch) are not visible in any frame on a cliff-top deck; even if rendered, they leave 3.5 m gaps over a 120 m drop.
No moon or sea proxy exists, so the reveal camera (target 175, 95, 130) shows empty sky. A moon disc and a cloud-sea plane are needed to judge this space at all.
The sake counter, cushions and paving are all inside a solid volume.
